title: How Virat Kohli's YouTube Clips Helped Nathan McSweeney Beat India's Spinners
excerpt: The Australia A batter studied Kohli and Steve Smith footage to crack India's spin, scoring 194 runs at 64.66 to win Player of the Series in Australia A's 2-1 ODI win over India A.
body:
• Australia A batter Nathan McSweeney revealed he studied Virat Kohli's batting videos on YouTube — alongside footage of Steve Smith — to learn how to play spin in Indian conditions.
  • The homework paid off: McSweeney piled up 194 runs in three innings (average 64.66, strike rate 83.62), winning Player of the Series as Australia A beat India A 2-1 in Puducherry.
  • Australia A lost the preceding four-day series 1-0 but stormed back in the one-dayers, winning the first two matches by 125 and 69 runs; India avoided a whitewash with a 49-run win in Sunday's final game.
  • The 27-year-old played all three of his Tests for Australia against India in 2024 — and admits the unofficial Test series this tour did not go to plan, with scores of 0, 35, 34, and 36.

PUDUCHERRY — When Nathan McSweeney needed a masterclass in playing spin, he turned to YouTube — and to Virat Kohli. The Australia A batter has revealed that studying the former India captain's batting footage online was a cornerstone of his preparation for the one-day series against India A, a series he went on to dominate.

"I think obviously coming to India as an Australian, it's a heavy spin focus and you try and work hard and watch the great Indian players on how they play spin. [Watching] Virat Kohli on YouTube trying to study how he goes about it," McSweeney told the host broadcaster after the series ended on Sunday, adding that he also studied Steve Smith and other Australians who have succeeded in Indian conditions, alongside the data and analysis supplied by his team's support staff.

Context & Background

Australia A's tour of India began with disappointment: the visitors lost the two-match unofficial Test series 1-0, and McSweeney — who played three Tests for Australia against India in 2024 — admitted the first-class leg did not go to plan, managing only 0, 35, 34, and 36 across four innings.

https://x.com/CricCrazyJohns/status/2109259489593741693

The white-ball leg was a different story. Australia A won the first two one-dayers by 125 and 69 runs respectively, clinching the three-match series 2-1. India salvaged pride in the final match on Sunday with a 49-run win, but the series belonged to McSweeney. The 27-year-old opened with a blistering 123 off 135 balls, laced with 13 fours, and followed it with 32 and 39 — 194 runs in three innings at an average of 64.66 and a strike rate of 83.62.

Impact & Analysis

What made McSweeney's innings stand out was precisely what he had been studying: footwork. He used the depth of the crease, charged down the track to unsettle the spinners' lengths, deployed the sweep, and played with soft hands to rotate the strike into gaps — the full toolkit of a subcontinent-ready batter.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=rfWZueb6_JA

The episode says something larger about modern preparation. Touring sides now arrive armed with analysts and ball-by-ball data, but McSweeney's account is refreshingly old-school at its core: watch the masters, internalize the movement, execute in the middle. That the master in question is Kohli — a player the young Australian faced as an opponent — underscores how freely today's cricketers borrow across national lines. Winning a series in India, McSweeney noted, is "no easy feat by any international team"; doing it as the leading run-scorer, after a quiet Test series, makes the turnaround all the more notable.

Diaspora Angle

For cricket fans in the Indian diaspora, this is a familiar delight: an Australian batter publicly crediting Virat Kohli's technique as the textbook for surviving Indian spin — a small, genuine measure of how far Kohli's influence travels, even into rival dressing rooms.

What's Next

McSweeney's white-ball form will have reignited the conversation about his place in Australia's Test plans, particularly with another spin-heavy subcontinent tour always on the horizon. For India A, the 2-1 defeat will sharpen scrutiny of the spin attack ahead of the next home cycle. External reporting: myKhel, Latestly, Indian Economic Observer.
